cards.text: Judah has a new king in Jerusalem named Josiah, and friend, this king is YOUNG. Not young for a king. I mean young-young.

cards.question: How old is Josiah when he becomes king in Jerusalem?

cards.text: EIGHT years old, and he reigns thirty-one years. I've been around a whole lot longer than eight years and I still can't keep a group chat from going off the rails.

cards.question: So what kind of king does young Josiah turn out to be?

answers.text: He does what's right in the LORD's eyes
He does evil in the LORD's eyes
He follows whatever his advisers say

cards.text: He walks in the ways of his ancestor David, and he doesn't turn aside to the right or to the left. Me, I can't walk past an oven without swerving over to peek inside.

cards.question: In the eighth year of his reign, while he's still young, Josiah begins to seek the God of his ancestor David.

cards.text: Fast forward to Josiah's twelfth year as king. That's when he starts a big job in Judah and Jerusalem.

cards.question: In his twelfth year as king, what does Josiah start clearing out of Judah and Jerusalem?

cards.text: First up: the altars of the Baals. And this is NOT a send-a-memo kind of king.

cards.question: King Josiah stays back at the palace while the altars of the Baals come down.

cards.text: He cuts to pieces the incense altars that stood above the Baal altars. Then he turns to the Asherah poles, the carved idols and the cast images.

cards.question: Josiah shatters the Asherah poles and idols, crushes them to ___ and scatters it over the ___ of the people who sacrificed to them.

cards.text: Then he burns the bones of the priests on their altars, and Judah and Jerusalem are cleansed. I spent years in a junk drawer nobody ever cleaned out, and this man just cleaned out a whole kingdom.

cards.question: Once Judah and Jerusalem are cleansed, Josiah stops right there.

cards.text: He does the same in the cities of Manasseh, Ephraim and Simeon, all the way to Naphtali, and in the ruins around them. Altars torn down, Asherah poles torn down, idols crushed to powder, all through the land of Israel.

cards.question: With the land of Israel cleared out, where does Josiah go next?

cards.text: Now it's the eighteenth year of Josiah's reign, and to cleanse the land and the temple, he sends out three men. Shaphan son of Azaliah, Maaseiah the governor of the city, and Joah son of Joahaz, the recorder.

cards.question: What does King Josiah send Shaphan, Maaseiah and Joah to do?

answers.text: Repair the house of the LORD
Count the fighting men of Judah

cards.text: So the three men head out with the money that had been brought into the house of God. Somebody's about to be handed a LOT of money.

cards.question: Who do Shaphan, Maaseiah and Joah give the money for the house of God to?
Who had collected the money that was brought into the house of God?

answers.text: The Levites who guarded the doors
The king's officials in the cities

cards.question: All the money for the house of God came from the people of Jerusalem alone.

cards.text: It came from Manasseh, Ephraim and all the remnant of Israel, plus all Judah and Benjamin and the people of Jerusalem. Everybody chipped in, which is more than you can say for most office birthday collections.
The money goes to the men supervising the work, and they pass it on to the workmen restoring and repairing the house of the LORD.

cards.question: With the money, the carpenters and builders buy dressed ___ and timbers.

cards.text: The timbers and beams are for buildings the kings of Judah had allowed to deteriorate. Those kings treated the place like a check engine light: "Eh, I'll get to it."

cards.question: Now that the materials are in, the men do the work ___.

cards.text: Four Levites oversee the men: Jahath and Obadiah, descendants of Merari, and Zechariah and Meshullam, descendants of Kohath.

cards.question: The other Levites in charge of the laborers are all skilled with musical instruments.

cards.text: Those Levites are over the laborers and supervise everyone doing the work, task by task. Picture a job site run by the musicians, and friend, the work is getting DONE.

cards.question: Besides supervising the workers, what do some of the Levites serve as?

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave Josiah for now. Hang on to your apron, friend, because this story is far from done.

findings.problem: The setup line "this is NOT a send-a-memo kind of king" tells the baker that Josiah doesn't stay back. That rules out True on card 10, which asks whether he stays back at the palace while the Baal altars come down.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "ashes" is close to the right answer "dust" for the first blank. A baker could argue that crushed idols scattered over graves were ashes, especially with the burning in 34:5 right after.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The setup says the three men are sent "to cleanse the land and the temple." That points straight to the temple and rules out both wrong answers on card 2, "Rebuild the wall of Jerusalem" and "Count the fighting men of Judah," since neither is about the temple.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: "Somebody's about to be handed a LOT of money" says how much money there was, and 34:9 never says. It's stated as part of the story, not as a joke.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The closing line nearly copies the doc's example. "And that's where we'll leave Josiah for now" matches the example's "And that's where we'll leave it for now," and the rest follows the same shape ("friend, this story is far from done").

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.

findings.problem: Card 16 is only the line saying the story isn't over. It tells no verse but cites 2 Chronicles 34:13, which card 15 already covers. The citation rule says to cite exactly what the card uses, but this card uses no verse.
findings.question: When the last story card is only the line saying the story isn't over, which verses should it cite, if any?
